concept.name: AUDIT_REPORT
concept.human_rationale:
================================================================================ Unleashed 153 - FULL PATCH AUDIT REPORT Files: AudioStream.cpp, CubebUtils.cpp, FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp, PDMFactory.cpp, DecoderTraits.cpp, RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp Cross-referenced against: MEDIA_PATCHES.md, Audio_video.txt ================================================================================
CONFIRMED CORRECT ----------------- - CubebUtils.cpp: GetVolumeScale() correctly clamps to minimum 4.0x - CubebUtils.cpp: InitPreferredSampleRate() hard-locks to 48000 Hz - PDMFactory.cpp: kHardwareVideoDecodeOnly = true propagates through SupportsMimeType, Supports, and CreateDecoder correctly - DecoderTraits.cpp: Blacklist fires for av01, vp8, vp9, vp09, hev1, hvc1 - FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp: PATCH in CreateImageVAAPI does return MediaResult(NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR) for failed surface exports - RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp: IsSurfaceDescriptorValid check and NS_WARNING are present as described
================================================================================ BUG 1 — CRITICAL (AudioStream.cpp) THE SOFT-KNEE LIMITER IS IN THE WRONG PLACE AND DOES NOTHING USEFUL ================================================================================
CLAIM (MEDIA_PATCHES.md + Audio_video.txt): The soft-knee limiter protects against distortion caused by the 4.0x volume boost from CubebUtils.
REALITY: The limiter runs inside DataCallback() on the raw normalized samples produced by GetUnprocessed() or GetTimeStretched(). These samples are in the [-1.0, 1.0] range at this point in the pipeline.
The 4.0x gain is applied LATER, by cubeb itself, via:
AudioStream::SetVolume(double aVolume) { cubeb_stream_set_volume(aVolume * CubebUtils::GetVolumeScale()) }
cubeb_stream_set_volume multiplies the samples it receives FROM DataCallback by the volume factor before sending them to the OS/hardware.
Signal flow: DataCallback fills buffer (samples in -1.0 to +1.0) --> LIMITER clamps at 0.95 / hard-caps at 0.99 <-- runs HERE --> cubeb_stream_set_volume multiplies by 4.0x <-- gain applied HERE --> OS/DAC receives values up to ±3.96 <-- clips HERE
Result: A sample that the limiter "protected" at 0.99 becomes 3.96 after the 4.0x multiplication. A sample at the original 0.25 level becomes 1.0 (just clipping). Any pre-gain sample above 0.25 will clip hard at the OS/hardware level.
To actually protect against 4.0x clipping, the limiter threshold would need to be 1.0 / 4.0 = 0.25, not 0.95. As written, the limiter is architecturally meaningless — it operates on pre-gain signal and the gain is applied downstream by a component it cannot see.
Additionally, the behaviour of cubeb_stream_set_volume with a value > 1.0 is undefined by the cubeb API. Some backends (PulseAudio) support pre-amplification; others (CoreAudio, WASAPI) may cap at 1.0 silently, meaning the 4.0x boost does not function at all on those platforms.
IMPACT: The entire audio protection mechanism is non-functional. On platforms where the 4.0x boost does apply, audio will clip hard at the OS/hardware level on any signal louder than 25% of full scale.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 2 — MINOR (AudioStream.cpp) WRONG GAIN VALUE IN PATCH COMMENT ================================================================================
CLAIM: Limiter is "tuned for maximum power" handling a "4.0x gain boost".
REALITY: The PATCH comment in AudioStream.cpp reads:
"Replaces hard clipping with a smooth polynomial curve to handle the 2.0x volume boost without harsh harmonic distortion."
The comment says 2.0x. CubebUtils delivers 4.0x. This is either a stale copy from an earlier version of the patch or indicates the two files were written independently without being reconciled. Either way, someone reading the code cannot trust the comment.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 3 — MODERATE (FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp) FRAME POOL IS NOT UNIFORMLY 16 ACROSS ALL PATHS ================================================================================
CLAIM (both .md and .txt): "Standardized the frame pool size to 16 across all paths (VA-API, Vulkan, V4L2, SW-Upload)."
REALITY: Path Code Actual behaviour ----------- ----------------------------------------- ---------------- V4L2 MakeUnique<VideoFramePool<>>(16) Exactly 16 OK SW-Upload MakeUnique<VideoFramePool<>>(16) Exactly 16 OK VA-API MakeUnique<VideoFramePool<>>( "At least 16" std::max(context->initial_pool_size,16)) Vulkan MakeUnique<VideoFramePool<>>( "At least 16" std::max(context->initial_pool_size,16))
On the two paths that matter most for H.264 ASIC decode (VA-API and Vulkan), the pool size is the LARGER of 16 and whatever AVHWFramesContext::initial_pool_size reports. If the Intel driver reports a preferred pool of 24 or 32 frames, the pool will be 24 or 32.
The documentation's claim of "UMA-Aware Saturation" and "preventing RAM starvation" only holds if the pool stays at 16. With std::max, the pool can silently grow beyond that ceiling under any driver that prefers a larger pool, which is exactly the RAM starvation scenario being protected against on shared-memory Ivy Bridge hardware.
IMPACT: RAM starvation protection is unreliable on the two primary hardware decode paths. The two paths that are capped correctly (V4L2, SW-Upload) are the secondary or fallback paths.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 4 — MINOR-TO-MODERATE (FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp) std::abort() WAS NOT REMOVED — ONE COPY REMAINS ================================================================================
CLAIM (MEDIA_PATCHES.md): "Replaced std::abort() with MediaResult(NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_FATAL_ERR) to strictly forbid software fallback without causing tab crashes."
REALITY: A std::abort() call remains in the file in the VA-API hardware capability enumeration path:
VAStatus status = vaQueryConfigProfiles(mDisplay, profiles, &numProfiles); if (status != VA_STATUS_SUCCESS) { FFMPEG_LOG(" vaQueryConfigProfiles() failed %s", vaErrorStr(status)); std::abort(); // <-- still here }
This is a different call site from the surface-creation path that was patched, but the blanket claim that abort() was eliminated is false. A vaQueryConfigProfiles failure — which can occur if the VA-API driver is in a degraded state — will still call abort() and kill the GPU process, exactly the behaviour the patch set claimed to have eliminated.
IMPACT: Process crash on VA-API driver failure during capability query.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 5 — MODERATE (FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp) SOFTWARE FALLBACK LOOPHOLE VIA IsDecodingSlow() ================================================================================
CLAIM: "Hardware-Only Video Decode Fortress" — 0% CPU work for video.
REALITY: The following code exists untouched in the patched file:
if (mDecodeStats.IsDecodingSlow() && !StaticPrefs::media_ffmpeg_disable_software_fallback()) { FFMPEG_LOG("HW decoding is slow, switching back to SW decode"); return MediaResult(NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_DECODE_ERR, ...); }
When hardware decoding is measured as too slow (frame drops), the decoder returns NS_ERROR_DOM_MEDIA_DECODE_ERR. The media pipeline interprets this as a signal to restart the decoder without hardware acceleration.
The StaticPref media.ffmpeg.disable_software_fallback controls this behaviour. It is NOT set anywhere in the patch set. Its default value is false, meaning the software fallback path is active.
Under sustained load on Ivy Bridge — which is exactly the scenario this patch set is trying to manage — hardware decoding can be declared "slow", and the decoder will escape the hardware-only policy through this exit. The fortress has a door and it is unlocked.
IMPACT: Under load, video can escape to software decoding despite all the PDMFactory and DecoderTraits gates. The pref media.ffmpeg.disable_software_fallback = true was never set.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 6 — MODERATE (PDMFactory.cpp) STATIC SupportsMimeType PATCH BLOCKS AUDIO CODEC QUERIES ================================================================================
CLAIM: Hardware-only gate applies to video only; audio is unaffected.
REALITY: The static overload of PDMFactory::SupportsMimeType has this structure:
const TrackSupportSet supports = GetTrackSupport(aLocation);
if (supports.contains(TrackSupport::DecodeVideo)) { // PATCH if (MP4Decoder::IsH264(aMimeType)) { return MCSInfo::GetDecodeSupportSet(MediaCodec::H264, aSupported); } return DecodeSupportSet{}; // <-- returns here for ALL non-H264 }
if (supports.contains(TrackSupport::DecodeAudio)) { // AAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis, FLAC handling... }
The PATCH returns an EMPTY DecodeSupportSet for any MIME type that is not H264, including audio MIME types like "audio/mp4" or "audio/mpeg", whenever the queried process supports DecodeVideo.
In the RDD process, TrackSupportSet commonly contains both DecodeVideo and DecodeAudio. When this function is called to check audio codec support for that process, it enters the DecodeVideo branch, finds the audio MIME type is not H264, and returns empty. The DecodeAudio branch is never reached.
IMPACT: Audio codec support is reported as zero for any remote decoder process that also handles video. This can cause audio tracks in video files to be treated as unsupported, breaking audio/video synchronised playback.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 7 — CRITICAL (RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp) PATCH DROPS ALL FRAMES WHEN NO COMPOSITOR BRIDGE EXISTS ================================================================================
CLAIM: "Drops frames with invalid GPU descriptors."
REALITY: The SurfaceDescriptor sd variable is declared uninitialized (default state) before the compositor block:
SurfaceDescriptor sd; // default — type is T__None (invalid)
if (mKnowsCompositor) { // ... if (texture) { sd = remoteSD; // only set here } }
// PATCH if (!IsSurfaceDescriptorValid(sd)) { NS_WARNING("..."); continue; // drops frame }
When mKnowsCompositor is null — which happens whenever no direct VideoBridge connection to the compositor was established — sd is never assigned. IsSurfaceDescriptorValid() on a default SurfaceDescriptor returns false. Every single decoded frame is silently dropped.
mKnowsCompositor is null in several real scenarios: - RDD process without a direct GPU compositor bridge (fallback init) - Post-crash GPU process recovery during reinitialization window - Any decode location other than GPU process (MF CDM process, etc.)
The same drop also fires when mKnowsCompositor IS set but texture acquisition fails (texture = nullptr), blocking the original fallback behaviour that would have serialised the frame via shmem IPC.
The original code had downstream handling for both cases. The PATCH inserts before that code and short-circuits it entirely.
IMPACT: In any non-GPU-compositor path, video produces no frames and no error is surfaced to the player. Manifests as a frozen or black frame with audio continuing — extremely hard to diagnose because no fatal error is returned, only an NS_WARNING.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 8 — MODERATE (RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp) COLOR SPACE METADATA IS HARDCODED AND NEVER READ FROM THE DECODED FRAME ================================================================================
CLAIM: No explicit claim about colour space; implied correctness.
REALITY: Four colour space variables are declared with defaults and passed directly to RemoteImageHolder without ever being populated:
YUVColorSpace YUVColorSpace = gfx::YUVColorSpace::Default; ColorSpace2 colorPrimaries = gfx::ColorSpace2::UNKNOWN; TransferFunction transferFunction = gfx::TransferFunction::BT709; ColorRange colorRange = gfx::ColorRange::LIMITED;
// ... (no code that reads these from video->mImage) ...
RemoteImageHolder(... sd, YUVColorSpace, colorPrimaries, transferFunction, colorRange)
The original code before these patches presumably queried video->mImage for its actual colour space metadata before building RemoteImageHolder. That query was either removed or never included in the PATCH.
As a result, every frame is rendered as BT.709 / LIMITED range regardless of its actual metadata. Affected content: - Standard-definition content encoded in BT.601 (wrong green/skin tones) - Any full-range content (FULL range clipped to LIMITED — washed out) - HDR content mastered in BT.2020 (completely wrong colour gamut)
For modern H.264 web video at 1080p, BT.709/LIMITED is the most common combination, so this may not be obvious. But any SD stream, full-range encode, or HDR-tagged stream will render with visually wrong colours.
IMPACT: Incorrect colour rendering for a wide category of H.264 content. Will appear as slightly wrong skin tones, washed-out colours, or completely off-gamut colours depending on source material.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
================================================================================ BUG 9 — MINOR (DecoderTraits.cpp) CANPLAY_MAYBE / CANPLAY_NO INCONSISTENCY FOR BLOCKED CONTAINERS ================================================================================
CLAIM: Browsers are forced to serve H.264 because non-H.264 is rejected.
REALITY: The PATCH in CanHandleCodecsType only fires when aType.ExtendedType().HaveCodecs() is true — i.e., when an explicit codec string is present in the MIME type.
For container-only queries (no codec string), the code falls through to the container-level checks, which still return CANPLAY_MAYBE for WebM:
video.canPlayType('video/webm') --> "maybe" (unblocked) video.canPlayType('video/webm; codecs="vp9"') --> "" (blocked)
HTML5 video players frequently probe both forms. A player that sees "maybe" for video/webm will attempt to load a VP9 stream, make a network request, begin buffering, and only then receive a rejection at the codec level. This is worse than returning "" immediately — it wastes bandwidth and causes a visible loading failure instead of a clean silent fallback to H.264.
The correct fix would be to also block the container-only query for video/webm (and other blocked containers) at the CanHandleMediaType level, or remove WebMDecoder from the supported type list entirely.
IMPACT: Some HTML5 players will attempt VP9 streams, fail mid-load, and produce a buffering failure or visible error before retrying H.264.
================================================================================
SUMMARY TABLE ================================================================================
# File Severity Description -- ----------------------- ---------- ------------------------------------ 1 AudioStream.cpp CRITICAL Limiter is pre-gain; provides zero protection against 4.0x clipping 2 AudioStream.cpp Minor Comment says 2.0x, system uses 4.0x 3 FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp Moderate VA-API/Vulkan pool is std::max(n,16) not exactly 16 as documented 4 FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp Minor-Mod std::abort() not removed from vaQueryConfigProfiles path 5 FFmpegVideoDecoder.cpp Moderate IsDecodingSlow() SW fallback gate is active; pref never disabled 6 PDMFactory.cpp Moderate Static SupportsMimeType returns empty for audio MIME types in video-capable processes 7 RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp CRITICAL All frames dropped silently when mKnowsCompositor is null 8 RemoteVideoDecoder.cpp Moderate Colour space metadata hardcoded; never read from decoded frame 9 DecoderTraits.cpp Minor CANPLAY_MAYBE / CANPLAY_NO mismatch for WebM without explicit codec string
================================================================================
NOTES FOR DISCUSSION ================================================================================
The two CRITICAL bugs are structurally related:
Bug 1 (limiter) exists because the gain stage and the protection stage are in different components (AudioStream vs CubebUtils/cubeb) with no shared awareness of each other. The fix requires either moving the gain into DataCallback where it can be limited together, or lowering the limiter threshold to 1.0/scale (0.25 at 4.0x) and accepting the loss of dynamic range that implies.
Bug 7 (frame drop) exists because the zero-copy enforcement was inserted as a single gate that does not distinguish between "frame has no GPU surface" and "frame was never going to have a GPU surface because there is no compositor bridge." The fix requires checking mKnowsCompositor before applying the gate, or restructuring the enforcement to only apply when the architecture expects GPU-backed surfaces.
Bugs 5 and 6 are policy gaps: the hardware-only intent is documented and partially implemented, but two code paths were not accounted for.
Bug 8 is a regression that was likely introduced by omission — the colour space query code was probably not in scope for the PATCH but was adjacent to code that was changed, and the variable population was lost.
================================================================================ END OF REPORT ================================================================================
